prompt: In Massachusetts, a driver of any age fails a chemical (breath or blood) test at what blood alcohol content (BAC)?
explanation: All drivers fail a chemical test at a BAC of 0.08 or greater. Drivers under 21 also face administrative penalties starting at 0.02.

prompt: A 19-year-old Massachusetts driver is stopped and has a BAC of 0.03. What happens under the state's zero-tolerance law?
choices: Nothing, because the limit for all drivers is 0.08
The driver gets only a written warning for a first stop
The driver loses their license, because the under-21 limit is 0.02
Penalties apply only at 0.05 or higher for drivers 18 to 20
explanation: Massachusetts has a zero-tolerance law: a driver under 21 caught with a BAC as low as 0.02 loses their license. 0.08 is the criminal standard, but under-21 penalties start at 0.02.

prompt: A 30-year-old with no prior OUI offenses refuses a breath test after an OUI arrest. How long is the license suspension for the refusal?
explanation: Under the Implied Consent Law, a driver over 21 with no prior OUI offenses who refuses a chemical test is suspended for 180 days. Three years applies when the driver has one prior OUI.

prompt: A 19-year-old with no prior OUI offenses refuses a chemical test. What suspension does the refusal bring?
explanation: Drivers age 18 to 21 who refuse a chemical test face three years plus an extra 180 days. The extra 180 days can be waived on a first OUI case by entering an approved alcohol education program.

prompt: A 35-year-old driver fails a breath test with a BAC of 0.09. What happens to the license before the court case ends?
choices: It is suspended for 30 days or until the case ends, whichever is shorter
It is suspended for one full year right away
Nothing happens until the driver is convicted
It is suspended for 180 days no matter what the court decides
explanation: For drivers over 21, a failed chemical test brings a 30-day suspension or a suspension until the court case ends, whichever is shorter. The court then sets any further penalty.

prompt: What is the license suspension for a first conviction of operating under the influence (OUI) in Massachusetts?
explanation: A first OUI conviction carries a one-year license suspension. The court may let you take an alcohol education course to reduce it. Two years is the suspension for a second offense.

prompt: Your passenger is holding an open can of beer while you drive. Under Massachusetts law, what is true?
choices: It is illegal; an open alcoholic drink may not be in the vehicle even if someone else holds it
It is legal as long as the driver is not drinking
It is legal if the passenger is 21 or older
It is illegal only if the can is in the cup holder
explanation: You may not have an open alcoholic drink inside the vehicle, even if someone else is holding it. A conviction brings a $100 to $500 fine.

prompt: A 19-year-old tries to buy beer at a store. What license penalty does Massachusetts law set for this?
choices: A warning on a first offense
A one-year license suspension only if they were driving
explanation: If you are under 21 and you buy, or try to buy, alcohol, your license is suspended for 180 days. Driving does not have to be involved.

prompt: A 17-year-old fails a chemical test while driving. What license suspension follows?
choices: 30 days plus an additional one year
explanation: Drivers under 18 who fail a chemical test are suspended for 30 days plus one additional year. On a first OUI case, the extra year can be cut to 180 days by entering an approved alcohol education program. Three years plus one year is the penalty for refusing the test.

prompt: In Massachusetts, a commercial motor vehicle driver commits a disqualifying offense at what alcohol concentration?
explanation: State law disqualifies a person from driving a commercial motor vehicle for at least a year for operating one with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more. That is half the 0.08 limit for other drivers.

prompt: What is the minimum age to apply for a Class D learner's permit in Massachusetts?
explanation: You must be at least 16 to apply for a Class D or Class M learner's permit. No one under 16 may drive in Massachusetts, even with an out-of-state license.

prompt: The Massachusetts learner's permit exam has 25 questions. How many must you answer correctly to pass?
explanation: You must answer 18 of the 25 questions correctly within the 25-minute time limit to pass.

prompt: What is the earliest age at which a Massachusetts teen can get a Class D driver's license (a Junior Operator License)?
explanation: You can get a permit at 16, but you may not get a Class D license until you are at least 16 1/2, have held the permit for six months, and have finished driver's education.

prompt: An applicant under 18 must hold a learner's permit for how long before taking the road test?
explanation: Junior Operator applicants must hold a valid permit for at least six consecutive months and keep a clean record for six months. A suspension restarts the six months.

prompt: How many hours of supervised driving must a parent or guardian certify for a 17-year-old applying for a license (with no skills development program)?
explanation: Applicants 16 1/2 to 18 must complete 40 hours of supervised driving. It drops to 30 hours only if they completed a driver skills development program.

prompt: Who may supervise a driver holding a Class D learner's permit?
choices: Any licensed driver 18 or older seated anywhere in the car
A licensed driver at least 21 with one year of experience, in the front passenger seat
A licensed driver at least 25 with three years of experience
Any adult, licensed or not, in the front seat
explanation: The supervisor must be at least 21, hold a valid license from Massachusetts or another state, have at least one year of driving experience, and sit in the passenger seat next to you.

prompt: A 16-year-old with a learner's permit wants to practice driving at 12:30 a.m. with a licensed 25-year-old friend. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, because the friend is over 21
No; permit holders under 18 may not drive from 12:00 to 5:00 a.m. unless with a licensed parent or guardian
Yes, because the permit night limit starts at 1:00 a.m.
No; permit holders may not drive after sunset at all
explanation: A permit holder under 18 may not drive between 12:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian who is a licensed driver with at least one year of experience.

prompt: During what hours may a Junior Operator License (JOL) holder NOT drive unless accompanied by a parent or legal guardian?
explanation: A JOL holder may not drive between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. unless a parent or legal guardian is in the car. Breaking this rule can be charged as driving without being licensed.

prompt: A 17-year-old JOL holder drives home at 1:30 a.m. with her 23-year-old licensed cousin in the passenger seat. Which is true?
choices: She is breaking the night restriction; only a parent or legal guardian satisfies it
She is legal because the cousin is over 21
She is legal because the night restriction ends at 1:00 a.m.
She is legal because the night limit applies only on weekends
explanation: The JOL night restriction (12:30 to 5:00 a.m.) is lifted only by a parent or legal guardian in the car. A licensed adult cousin does not count.

prompt: Three months after getting her JOL, a 17-year-old wants to drive her 16-year-old friend to school with no one else in the car. Is this allowed?
choices: No; for the first six months she may not carry passengers under 18 who are not immediate family
Yes, passengers are allowed once she has her license
Yes, as long as it is during daylight
No; JOL holders may never carry passengers until 18
explanation: During the first six months with a JOL, you may not drive with any passenger under 18 (other than immediate family) unless a qualified driver at least 21 with one year of experience is beside you.

prompt: During the first six months of a JOL, which passenger may a 16 1/2-year-old drive with, with no adult present?
explanation: The six-month passenger restriction does not apply to immediate family members, so a younger brother may ride along. Non-family passengers under 18 need a qualified 21+ supervisor in the car.

prompt: What is the license suspension for a first violation of the JOL passenger or night restriction?
explanation: Violating the passenger or night restriction brings a 60-day suspension for a first offense, 180 days for a second, and one year after that. Second and later offenses also require a retraining course.

prompt: A 17-year-old Junior Operator is found responsible for a first speeding ticket. What happens to the license?
choices: Nothing, if the fine is paid on time
It is suspended for one year
explanation: A Junior Operator license is suspended for 90 days for a first speeding citation and one year for any later one. Reinstatement requires a new permit exam, a retraining course, and a new road test.

prompt: An adult driver is found responsible for three speeding violations within 12 months. What happens?
choices: The driver must pay a $500 surcharge but keeps the license
The license is suspended for one year
Nothing, unless one of the violations caused a crash
The license is automatically suspended for 30 days
explanation: Three speeding violations within a 12-month period automatically suspend your license for 30 days. The 12 months start when you pay or are found responsible for the first citation.

prompt: A driver has three surchargeable events within two years. What does the RMV require?
choices: Nothing until there are seven events
Completing a Driver Retraining course within 90 days, or the license is suspended
explanation: Three surchargeable events within two years require the Massachusetts Driver Retraining course within 90 days. If you don't finish it, your license is suspended until you do.

prompt: How many surchargeable events within three years cause an automatic 60-day license suspension?
explanation: Seven surchargeable events within a three-year period mean an automatic 60-day suspension. Three events within two years trigger the retraining course requirement.

prompt: Massachusetts counts 'surchargeable events' on your driving record toward possible suspension. What are they?
choices: Any crash, whether or not you were at fault
explanation: Motor vehicle violations and at-fault crashes are surchargeable events. Each one counts toward a possible suspension and can raise your insurance under the Safe Driver Insurance Plan. Parking tickets are handled by cities and towns.

prompt: What are the minimum auto liability insurance limits in Massachusetts?
explanation: Massachusetts minimum limits are $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident for bodily injury, plus $30,000 for property damage.

prompt: If you fail a Massachusetts road test, how long must you wait before taking another?
choices: You may retest the next day
explanation: If you fail a road test or miss your scheduled test, you must wait at least 14 days before taking another one.

prompt: You move to Massachusetts and become a resident. How long can you keep driving on your old state's license?
choices: There is no grace period; you must get a Massachusetts license
explanation: If you become a Massachusetts resident, you must obtain a Massachusetts license to keep your driving privileges. There is no grace period.

prompt: You are 25 and stopped at a red light. May you pick up your phone to read a text?
choices: Yes, because the car is not moving
No; handheld use is not allowed at red lights or stop signs
Yes, if the light has been red for over 30 seconds
Yes, for reading only, not for sending
explanation: Handheld device use is allowed only when the vehicle is stationary and not in a public travel lane. It is not allowed at red lights or stop signs, and reading messages while driving is banned.

prompt: How may a driver 18 or older use a cell phone while driving in Massachusetts?
choices: Only in hands-free mode, with the phone mounted, touching it only to start hands-free mode
Holding the phone, as long as it is on speaker
Any way, if the driver has had a license for one year
Holding it for calls but not for texts
explanation: Drivers 18 and older may use devices only in hands-free mode. The device can't be held, can be touched only to activate hands-free mode, and must be mounted to the windshield, dashboard or center console.

prompt: A 17-year-old driver has a phone mounted on the dashboard. May they take a call in hands-free mode?
choices: No; drivers under 18 may not use any mobile device while driving, except to report an emergency
Yes, hands-free calls are allowed for every driver
Yes, if a parent is calling
explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use any mobile electronic device for any reason while driving, even hands-free. The only exception is reporting an emergency.

prompt: What is the fine for a first offense of using a handheld device while driving in Massachusetts?
explanation: Fines are $100 for a first offense, $250 plus a distracted-driving program for a second, and $500 plus an insurance surcharge and the program for a third or later offense.

prompt: When can Massachusetts police fine a driver for not wearing a seat belt?
choices: Anytime an officer sees an unbelted driver
Never; Massachusetts has no adult seat belt law
Only when the driver has been stopped for another traffic violation
explanation: Massachusetts requires belts for everyone, but you can only be fined for the seat belt law when you are stopped for a traffic violation (secondary enforcement). The fine is $25.

prompt: A 14-year-old passenger is not wearing a seat belt and the car is stopped for speeding. Who can be fined $25 for the belt violation?
choices: The vehicle's owner, if not driving
No one, because passengers under 16 are exempt
explanation: A driver can be fined $25 for each passenger age 12, 13, 14 or 15 who is not wearing a seat belt. Passengers 16 and older are fined themselves.

prompt: Until when must a Massachusetts child ride in a federally approved child passenger restraint?
choices: Until they are at least 6 years old or 50 pounds
Until they are at least 10 years old
Until they are at least 4 years old and 40 pounds
Until they are at least 8 years old or at least 57 inches tall
explanation: Children must use a child passenger restraint until they are at least eight years old or at least fifty-seven inches tall. After that, they must wear a properly fitted seat belt.

prompt: A 7-year-old is 58 inches tall. Under Massachusetts law, how may the child ride?
choices: In a booster seat until age 8, regardless of height
In a booster seat until 80 pounds
With a properly worn seat belt, because the child is over 57 inches
Only in the back seat in a car seat
explanation: The law requires a child restraint until a child is at least 8 OR at least 57 inches tall. A 58-inch child meets the height rule and must wear a seat belt correctly.

prompt: What does Massachusetts law say about headphones while driving?
choices: Headphones are allowed at low volume
They are illegal, but drivers 18 or older may use one earpiece for a cell phone
Drivers of any age may use one earpiece
Wireless earbuds are allowed in both ears
explanation: Wearing headphones or any device that restricts your attention to the environment is illegal. Drivers 18 or older may use one earplug for a cell phone.

prompt: You are driving 40 mph in a heavy rainstorm on a highway posted at 50 mph. Can you be ticketed for speed?
choices: No, because you are 10 mph under the limit
No, posted limits are the only legal standard
Yes; you must slow down to a speed that is safe for conditions
Only if you cause a crash
explanation: Under the fundamental speed law, you must never drive faster than is safe. The manual says 40 mph in a heavy rainstorm on a 50 mph highway can get you a ticket.

prompt: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Massachusetts school zone?
explanation: The speed limit on roads near schools is 20 mph. It may be posted with flashing yellow lights or for certain hours.

prompt: With no speed limit sign posted, what is the limit in a thickly settled or business district in Massachusetts?
choices: 30 mph (or 25 mph where signs show it)
explanation: Unless posted otherwise, 30 mph is the limit in a thickly settled or business district. Some communities have adopted a 25 mph limit, posted at their entrances.

prompt: With no speed limit posted, what is the maximum reasonable speed on a road (not a highway) outside a thickly settled or business district?
explanation: Unless posted, driving over 40 mph outside a thickly settled or business district is not reasonable and proper. On a highway outside such districts, the figure is 50 mph.

prompt: With no speed limit posted, what is the maximum reasonable speed on a highway outside a thickly settled or business district?
explanation: Unless posted otherwise, over 50 mph on a highway outside a thickly settled or business district is not reasonable and proper.

prompt: What is the highest speed limit you will find on Massachusetts limited-access highways such as interstates?
explanation: Limited-access highways, like interstates, have speed limits from 50 to 65 mph in Massachusetts.

prompt: What is the minimum speed on the Massachusetts Turnpike?
explanation: There is a 40 mph minimum speed on the Massachusetts Turnpike. Even where no minimum is posted, police may order a driver who is slowing traffic to the side of a state highway.

prompt: What following distance does the Massachusetts manual give as the minimum in good conditions?
explanation: Use the three-second rule as a minimum in good road conditions and moderate traffic. Count more for added safety.

prompt: How much following distance should you leave behind a motorcycle?
choices: Three seconds, the same as a car
explanation: Use a four-second following distance behind a motorcycle, compared with three seconds behind other motor vehicles.

prompt: How much space should you keep between your car and heavy equipment such as a dump truck or tractor?
explanation: Keep at least ten seconds between your vehicle and heavy equipment like dump trucks and tractors. These vehicles carry more weight and need more room to stop.

prompt: A driver is caught going 73 mph where the limit is 55 mph. Using the manual's example, what is the speeding fine?
explanation: The base fine covers the first 10 mph over ($105 in the manual's example), plus $10 for each mph above that: 8 x $10 = $80, for a total of $185.

prompt: When may you turn right on a steady red light in Massachusetts?
choices: Only when a green arrow appears
After slowing down, without stopping, if no one is coming
Never; right on red is illegal in Massachusetts
After a complete stop and yielding, unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted
explanation: You must come to a complete stop and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles. Then you may turn right unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.

prompt: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Massachusetts?
choices: From any street, if no traffic is coming
From a two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping
explanation: You may turn left on red only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street. You must stop and yield first.

prompt: You are on a two-way street at a red light and want to turn left onto a one-way street. May you turn on red after stopping?
choices: Yes, because you are turning onto a one-way street
No; left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
Yes, if no NO TURN ON RED sign is posted
Yes, if you are in the far left lane
explanation: Massachusetts allows left turns on red only when both streets are one-way. Turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street on red is not allowed.

prompt: In Massachusetts, what does a steady red arrow pointing right mean?
choices: You may never turn right until it turns green
It means the same as a steady red light for that direction; you may turn after a full stop unless a sign prohibits it
You may turn right without stopping
explanation: A steady red arrow means the same as a steady red circle, but only for traffic going in the arrow's direction. The same turn-on-red rules apply in Massachusetts, though other states may differ.

prompt: How far before a turn must you signal on a regular road in Massachusetts?
explanation: Signal your turn at least 100 feet before making it. On a highway, signal at least 500 feet before a turn.

prompt: Your light is red and there is an empty green bicycle box painted in your lane in front of the crosswalk. Where must you stop?
choices: Inside the box, since no bicyclists are there
Anywhere, as long as you don't block the crosswalk
Behind the bicycle box, even though it is empty
explanation: Drivers must stop behind the bicycle box, even when it is empty, and wait for a green light. The box is reserved for bicyclists.

prompt: In Massachusetts, what does red-colored pavement in a travel lane indicate?
choices: A lane or stop for public transit such as buses or trolleys
A no-stopping zone near a school
explanation: Red pavement is used for travel lanes or station stops used by public transit, including buses, streetcars, trolleys, light rail and rapid transit.

prompt: A street has an advisory bicycle lane marked with dashed lines. What may a driver do?
choices: Never enter the lane for any reason
Use the lane space when necessary, but always yield to bicyclists first
Use the lane as a regular travel lane
Park in the lane outside rush hours
explanation: Advisory bicycle lanes are dashed to show that motor vehicles may use the lane space when necessary, but drivers must always yield to bicyclists first.

prompt: How are numbered Massachusetts state highway routes marked?
choices: With blue, red and white shields
With white rectangular signs with black letters and borders
explanation: In Massachusetts, numbered state highway routes are posted on white rectangular signs with black letters and borders. Blue, red and white shields mark interstate highways.

prompt: You are entering a Massachusetts rotary. Who has the right-of-way?
explanation: There are yield signs at rotary entrances. Always yield to vehicles already in the rotary (unless signs or police say otherwise) and to pedestrians.

prompt: A pedestrian using a white cane starts to cross the street in front of you. What does the White Cane Law require?
choices: Slow down and pass carefully behind the person
Honk lightly so the person knows you are there
Come to a complete stop and stay stopped until the person has crossed
explanation: The White Cane Law requires a complete stop for a blind pedestrian crossing the street. Stay stopped until they have safely crossed, and don't honk or wave them on.

prompt: Your light turns green, but a funeral procession is passing through the intersection against its red light. What should you do?
choices: Go, because you have the green light
Wait, unless you can cross without crossing the procession's path
explanation: Funeral processions have the right-of-way at intersections. You may not cross, even on a green light, unless you can do so without crossing the procession's path, and you may not join or cut into it.

prompt: In which direction does traffic travel in a Massachusetts rotary?
choices: Either direction, depending on the exit
Clockwise in small rotaries, counter-clockwise in large ones
explanation: Traffic travels counter-clockwise in a rotary. Yield to vehicles already in it, and use your right signal when you are ready to exit.

prompt: A multi-lane rotary has no lane signs. You want to make a three-quarter turn. Which lane should you enter from?
choices: The right lane, staying there the whole way
Either lane, then cut across at your exit
The left lane, then travel in the inner lane and exit into the right lane
explanation: With no signs, use the left lane to enter for a three-quarter turn or U-turn, travel through the middle or inner lane, and exit onto the right lane. For a quarter turn or to go straight, use the right lane throughout.

prompt: You miss your exit in a rotary. What should you do?
choices: Stop and wait for a gap to back up
Cut straight across the inner lanes to the exit
Stop in the rotary and signal
Check traffic and, if safe, go around again
explanation: If you miss your exit, don't get upset and don't stop in the rotary. If it is safe, go around again and position yourself to exit properly.

prompt: When is a U-turn NOT allowed in Massachusetts?
choices: Where you or other drivers cannot see 500 feet away, such as near a curve or hill crest
Within 100 feet of a stop sign
explanation: Do not make a U-turn at the crest of a hill, near a curve, or anywhere you or other drivers cannot see 500 feet away. Never make one where a NO U-TURN sign is posted.

prompt: You want to pass by crossing a broken yellow line. How far ahead must you be able to see clearly?
explanation: If you are crossing a broken yellow line to pass, you must be able to see clearly at least 400 feet in front of you.

prompt: While passing on a two-lane road, you must return to the right lane before an oncoming vehicle comes within what distance?
explanation: You must return to the right lane before any oncoming vehicle comes within 200 feet of you.

prompt: On a Massachusetts multiple-lane highway, which lanes may trucks and buses use?
choices: Only the left lane for passing
explanation: Trucks and buses can only drive in the two right-hand lanes: the far right for normal travel and the second lane for passing. Don't drive too slowly in that second lane.

prompt: On a Massachusetts expressway with three or more lanes in your direction, how should the lanes be used?
choices: Left lane for slower driving, right lane for passing
Right lane for slower driving, middle lane for faster driving, left lane for passing
explanation: Stay to the right and use the left lane for passing. With three or more lanes, use the far right for slower driving, the middle for faster driving, and the far left for passing.

prompt: On a four-lane highway (two lanes in your direction), you approach a police car stopped on the right shoulder with its lights flashing. What does the move-over law require?
choices: Slow down and, if safe, move to the lane not next to the stopped vehicle
Stop in your lane until the officer waves you on
Keep your speed and stay in your lane
Pass on the shoulder to the right of the police car
explanation: The move-over law requires you to slow to a reasonable and safe speed and, on a highway with at least four lanes, leave an open lane between you and the stopped emergency vehicle.

prompt: You approach a tow truck stopped with flashing lights, but heavy traffic stops you from moving over a lane. What must you do?
choices: Nothing; the law covers only police cars
Proceed with caution and reduce your speed
Stop until the tow truck leaves
Use the breakdown lane to pass
explanation: The move-over law also covers highway maintenance and recovery vehicles. If you cannot move over, you must still be cautious and reduce your speed.

prompt: Your car breaks down on a divided highway. Where should you place warning triangles or LED flares?
choices: 10 feet behind and 100 feet in front
10 feet and 100 feet behind your vehicle
explanation: On a divided highway, place warning triangles or LED flares 10 feet and 100 feet behind your vehicle. On a two-lane road with two-way traffic, also place one 100 feet in front.

prompt: Under Massachusetts' Vulnerable Road Users Law, how much space must you leave when passing a bicyclist?
explanation: When you pass a vulnerable road user, you must leave at least four feet. If safe, you may use part of the next lane or cross the center line, but you must obey the speed limit.

prompt: Which of these is a 'vulnerable road user' under Massachusetts law?
explanation: Vulnerable road users include pedestrians, roadside workers, bicyclists, horse riders, and people using wheelchairs, scooters, skateboards or roller skates. You must give them at least four feet when passing.

prompt: A school bus stopped on the other side of an undivided road has its red lights flashing and stop arm out. What must you do?
choices: Stop, and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing or the stop sign folds back
Slow to 20 mph and pass carefully
Continue, since the bus is on the other side
Stop, then go once the children are out of sight
explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop sign, no matter which side of the road you are on. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing or the sign folds back.

prompt: When do you NOT have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
choices: When it is on the other side of any four-lane road
When it is on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier between the directions
When it is on the other side of a road with a painted center turn lane
explanation: The only exception is a school bus stopped on the other side of a divided highway with a barrier between travel directions. Otherwise you must stop in either direction.

prompt: A trolley is stopped to let passengers on and off. How close may you drive to its passenger step?
choices: As close as needed if you go slowly
explanation: State law says you must not drive closer than eight feet to a trolley passenger step while it is letting passengers on or off.

prompt: What can a driver or passenger be fined for opening a car door into an oncoming bicyclist?
choices: There is no fine for this
explanation: Drivers and passengers can be fined up to $100 for opening a vehicle door into an oncoming bicycle. The manual recommends the Dutch Reach: open the door with your far hand so you turn and look.

prompt: Which is true about bicyclists on Massachusetts roads?
choices: They must always ride in the bike lane when one exists
They may use the full lane on any street (except posted limited-access highways), even if there is a bike lane
They may never ride two side by side
explanation: Bicyclists may use the full lane anywhere (except limited-access or express state highways posted against bicycles), even where there is a bike lane, and may ride two abreast.

prompt: A driver turning right hits a bicyclist who was riding legally to the right of traffic. Can the driver use the bike's position as a defense?
choices: Yes, bicycles must stay behind cars at intersections
Yes, if the driver used a turn signal
No; the law says the bicycle being to the right of traffic is not a defense
Only if the bicyclist was not wearing a helmet
explanation: Bicycles can legally ride to the right of motor vehicle traffic. The law says it is not a defense for a motorist causing a crash that the bicycle was to the right of other traffic.

prompt: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Massachusetts?
explanation: You may not park within ten feet of a fire hydrant or fire lane.

prompt: How close to an intersection may you park in Massachusetts?
explanation: Massachusetts prohibits parking within 20 feet of an intersection.

prompt: When parking along a curb in a business or residential district, how close must your vehicle be to the curb?
explanation: In a business or residential district, your vehicle must be no more than 12 inches from the curb, unless angled parking is allowed.

prompt: What is the fine for a first offense of parking in a space reserved for HP-DV (disability) parking without the right plate or placard?
explanation: The fine for a first offense of parking in an HP-DV space without disabled person or disabled veteran plates or a placard is $300. Wrongful use of a disability plate or placard is at least $500.

prompt: How close to a fire may you drive by or park?
explanation: It is illegal to drive by or park within 800 feet of a fire. Don't drive over an unprotected fire hose unless a firefighter or public safety official directs you to.

prompt: When must you use your headlights in Massachusetts?
choices: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
From one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise
explanation: You must use your headlights from one-half hour after sunset until one-half hour before sunrise, and at other times when visibility is poor.

prompt: It is a cloudy day and you turn on your windshield wipers because of rain. What does Massachusetts law require?
choices: Turn on your headlights and taillights; daytime running lights are not enough
explanation: The law requires headlights and taillights whenever you use your windshield wipers. Daytime running lights are not sufficient.

prompt: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle must you switch from high beams to low beams?
explanation: Lower your high beams when you are within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following.

prompt: You are using high beams on a dark road and come up behind another car. Within what distance must you dim them?
explanation: You must switch to low beams within 200 feet of a vehicle traveling ahead of you. The distance for oncoming vehicles is 500 feet.

prompt: You drive off after a snowstorm without clearing the snow from your car's roof, and it blows onto cars behind you. What can you be charged with?
choices: Nothing, if your windows are clear
explanation: Remove all ice and snow before driving, including the roof, hood and trunk. If snow blows into vehicles behind you, you can be charged with negligent operation.

prompt: Railroad crossing lights begin to flash as you approach. Where must you stop?
choices: At least 5 feet before the tracks
At least 15 feet before the light post or gate
At least 50 feet before the gate
explanation: If the lights begin to flash, you must stop at least 15 feet before the light post or gate and stay stopped until the gate rises and the lights stop.

prompt: When must you file a crash report in Massachusetts?
choices: Only when the police come to the scene
When there is $500 or more in property damage
When someone is killed or hurt, or there is $1,000 or more in property damage
explanation: You must report any crash that causes death or injury, or $1,000 or more in property damage.

prompt: How soon after a reportable crash must you file a written crash report with the RMV?
explanation: You must file a written crash report with the RMV within five days of the crash. Failing to report can lead to a fine and license suspension or revocation.

prompt: Where do copies of a Massachusetts Motor Vehicle Crash Operator Report go?
choices: The local police where the crash happened, your insurance company, and the RMV
The other driver's insurance company only
explanation: Send one copy to the local police department where the crash happened, one to your insurance company, and one to the RMV. Reporting only to your insurer is not enough.

prompt: You have a minor crash with no injuries and both cars can still be driven. What does the Driver Removal Law require?
choices: Leave the cars where they are until police arrive
Leave the scene and call your insurer later
Turn on hazards and wait in the travel lane
Move the vehicles out of the travel lanes to a safe place
explanation: If there are no injuries, the Driver Removal Law requires that vehicles be moved out of travel lanes to a safe location. You must still exchange information and stay at the scene.

prompt: An ambulance with its siren on is behind you on a city street. What must you do?
choices: Keep driving slowly in your lane
Pull to the left and stop
Speed up to get out of its way
Pull as close as possible to the right side and stop until it passes
explanation: For an emergency vehicle coming from any direction, pull as close as possible to the right side and stop until it has passed. Slowly rolling is not acceptable, and never stop in an intersection.

prompt: How close may you follow a fire truck that is responding to an alarm?
explanation: It is illegal to follow closer than 300 feet behind an emergency vehicle responding to an alarm.

prompt: In Massachusetts, drivers are 'Junior Operators' subject to JOL restrictions until what age?
explanation: Any driver between 16 1/2 and 18 is a Junior Operator, and the JOL restriction (code I) is on the licenses of all operators under 18. The passenger restriction can end sooner, after six months.

prompt: Which of these parking spots is illegal in Massachusetts?
choices: 10 inches from the curb on a residential street
explanation: You may not park in a crosswalk, in front of a driveway, or in front of a handicap-access ramp. The other spots meet the 20-foot intersection, 10-foot hydrant and 12-inch curb rules.

prompt: A 30-year-old driver has a phone mounted on the dashboard in hands-free mode. May they read a text message on it while driving?
choices: No; no driver may write, send or read an electronic message while driving
Yes, because the phone is mounted and not held
Yes, if the message is only one or two lines
Yes, but only while driving under 25 mph
explanation: Mounting the phone allows hands-free use, but mobile devices cannot be used to write, send or read an electronic message (texts, emails, instant messages or the internet) while driving. A mounted phone may still be used for GPS navigation.

prompt: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle in Massachusetts?
choices: Only riders with a learner's permit
Every operator and every passenger, at any age
Only riders under 21 or without health insurance
explanation: Massachusetts has a universal helmet law: every person operating or riding as a passenger on a motorcycle (or in a sidecar) must wear protective headgear. The only exception is riders 18+ in a permitted parade.

prompt: Your motorcycle has no windshield. What else does Massachusetts law require you to wear?
choices: Eyeglasses, goggles or a protective face shield
explanation: If a motorcycle has no windshield or screen, the operator must wear eyeglasses, goggles or a protective face shield.

prompt: You have a Class M learner's permit. May you carry a passenger?
choices: Yes, if the passenger is licensed
No, Class M permit holders may not carry passengers
Yes, if the passenger wears a helmet
explanation: A Class M learner's permit does not allow passengers. You must also ride only in daylight, wear a DOT helmet, and use eye protection unless the motorcycle has a windshield.

prompt: When may a Class M learner's permit holder ride?
explanation: A Class M permit holder may ride only during daylight hours, between sunrise and sunset.

prompt: In heavy, slow traffic, may a Massachusetts motorcyclist ride between lanes of cars?
choices: No, weaving or riding between lanes is illegal at any time
Yes, if traffic is fully stopped
explanation: It is illegal for a motorcycle operator to weave between lanes at any time. Riders must not ride along pavement lines between lanes of traffic.

prompt: How many motorcycles may ride side by side in one lane in Massachusetts?
choices: Any number, if the lane is wide
explanation: Massachusetts rules for motorcycles: ride no more than two abreast, and don't ride along pavement lines between lanes.

prompt: A 17-year-old wants a Class M license. What must they do?
choices: Complete the Massachusetts Rider Education Program (MREP) basic rider course
Pass the RMV Class M road test
Hold a Class D license for one year
explanation: Riders under 18 can't take an RMV Class M road test; they must complete the MREP basic rider course and also have a driver's education certificate.

prompt: What happens to the road test if you complete an approved Massachusetts Rider Education Program (MREP) course?
choices: You must still take two road tests
You may skip the permit exam but not the road test
You do not need to take the RMV Class M road test
explanation: Completing an RMV-approved MREP course means you don't need to take the RMV Class M road test.

prompt: You have failed the Class M road test twice. What must you do before scheduling another?
choices: Get a Class D license first
explanation: If you fail two Class M road tests, you must enroll in and complete a beginner rider course before you can schedule another test.

prompt: When may a motorcycle be ridden on a Massachusetts highway or expressway?
choices: Only if it can safely travel at the minimum posted speed
explanation: Unless your motorcycle can safely drive at the minimum posted speed, don't take it on highways or expressways.
